modules.name: ShortenerService
modules.responsibility: Core domain logic: generate unique short codes for long URLs, resolve codes back to long URLs, and enforce idempotency for repeated submissions of the same URL.

modules.name: CodeGenerator
modules.responsibility: Produce short, collision-resistant, URL-safe codes. Pluggable strategy (base62 counter, random, or hash-based) so the algorithm can change without touching domain logic.

modules.name: RedirectController
modules.responsibility: HTTP boundary for GET /{code}: resolve a code to its target URL, emit a 301/302 redirect, and fire a click event asynchronously. Returns 404 for unknown/expired codes.
interfaces:
class RedirectHandlerProtocol(Protocol):
    def handle(self, code: str, request: RequestMeta) -> RedirectResponse: ...

modules.name: StatsCollector
modules.responsibility: Record click events (code, timestamp, coarse referrer, hashed client identifier) and serve aggregate click statistics per short link. Writes are fire-and-forget; reads are aggregate-only.

modules.name: RateLimiter
modules.responsibility: Protect write/redirect endpoints from abuse using a token-bucket per client key (IP or API key). Stateless interface so backing store (in-memory vs distributed) is swappable.
interfaces:
class RateLimiterProtocol(Protocol):
    def check(self, key: str, *, cost: int = 1) -> RateDecision: ...

modules.name: ApiGateway
modules.responsibility: Top-level HTTP routing and middleware composition: wires rate limiting, request parsing, error mapping, and dispatch to ShortenerService and RedirectController. Single entry point for the service.
interfaces:
class ApiGatewayProtocol(Protocol):
    def route(self, request: HttpRequest) -> HttpResponse: ...

fields.name: creator_key_hash
fields.note: hash of API key/IP that created it, for abuse tracing

fields.name: client_hash
fields.note: HMAC(ip, rotating_salt) — pseudonymized, never raw IP

fields.name: user_agent_family
fields.note: parsed family (e.g. 'Chrome'), not full UA string

ux_flows.name: Shorten a URL
steps: Client sends POST /api/shorten with {long_url, optional custom_alias}
Gateway applies rate limit check on client key
CodeGenerator produces code (or validates custom_alias availability)
ShortLink persisted; service returns {code, short_url, expires_at}
ux_flows.success_criteria: 201 with a working short_url returned in a single request
i18n_considerations: Error messages localized via message keys
Accept internationalized domain names (IDN/punycode) in long_url

ux_flows.name: Follow a short link (redirect)
ux_flows.success_criteria: Redirect served in <50ms p95 with no blocking on stats write

ux_flows.name: View click statistics
steps: Gateway applies rate limit and (optional) auth
ux_flows.success_criteria: Aggregate stats returned; no per-user PII exposed

customer_journey: A developer or end user wants to share a long, unwieldy URL. They POST it to the shortener and immediately receive a compact short_url in one round trip — no signup required for the basic path. They share that link; recipients click it and are transparently redirected to the destination in well under a second, with each visit silently and privately counted. Later, the creator checks aggregate statistics (total clicks, daily trend, top referrer hosts) to gauge reach, seeing only pseudonymized aggregates — never individual visitor identities. Throughout, abusive callers are throttled by per-client rate limits so the service stays fast and available for everyone. The whole loop — shorten, share, redirect, measure — feels instant and trustworthy.

experience_metric.name: Shorten-to-share latency and effort
experience_metric.target: Obtain a working short URL in exactly 1 API request and <200ms p95; redirect served in <50ms p95
experience_metric.measurement: p95 latency on POST /api/shorten and GET /{code}; request count to first usable short_url

architecture_decisions.title: Pluggable short-code generation strategy behind a Protocol
architecture_decisions.context: Short codes must be unique, compact, URL-safe, and resistant to enumeration. Options include a monotonic base62 counter (shortest, but enumerable and leaks volume), random base62 with collision retry (non-enumerable, needs uniqueness check), and hash-of-URL (idempotent but longer/collision-prone). Each has different scaling, privacy, and idempotency trade-offs that may need to change post-launch.
architecture_decisions.decision: Define a CodeGeneratorProtocol with next_code()/is_valid() and inject the concrete strategy. Ship a random-base62-with-retry generator as the default; keep counter and hash strategies as alternative implementations selectable by config.
architecture_decisions.rationale: Isolating code generation behind an interface follows the Dependency Inversion and Open/Closed principles: the domain depends on an abstraction, and we can swap algorithms (e.g., move from random to a distributed ID scheme) without touching ShortenerService, persistence, or the API. Random-base62 default avoids the enumeration/volume-leak weakness of a counter.
consequences: Default random strategy requires a uniqueness check + retry loop on insert (bounded retries, then widen length)
Strategies are independently unit-testable with a seeded random source
Idempotency (same URL -> same code) is opt-in via the hash strategy, not guaranteed by default

architecture_decisions.title: Asynchronous, non-blocking click recording
architecture_decisions.context: Redirect latency is the headline experience metric, but every redirect should also produce a click stat. Writing the stat synchronously couples redirect latency to the stats store's availability and speed.
architecture_decisions.decision: RedirectController fires StatsCollector.record_click as fire-and-forget (background task/queue); the redirect response is returned before the write completes.
architecture_decisions.rationale: Decouples the hot redirect path from stats durability, keeping p95 redirect latency low and ensuring a stats outage cannot break redirects (availability over perfect counting).
consequences: Click counts are eventually consistent and may under-count on crash
Requires a bounded in-process queue or external queue with backpressure
Stats store outages degrade gracefully instead of failing redirects

threat_model.description: Attacker submits a malicious destination (phishing, malware, javascript: or file: schemes) to abuse the shortener's trust as a redirect cloak.
threat_model.mitigation: Whitelist http/https schemes, validate host, optional safe-browsing/blocklist check, and use 302 (not permanent) so malicious links can be revoked.

threat_model.description: Flood of shorten or redirect requests exhausts storage/compute or enumerates codes.
threat_model.mitigation: Per-client token-bucket rate limiting on all endpoints, max URL length, bounded code-generation retries, and non-enumerable random codes.

threat_model.description: Click statistics or raw logs expose visitor IP addresses / browsing behavior, leaking PII.
threat_model.mitigation: Never store raw IP; store only HMAC(ip, rotating salt). Stats API returns aggregates only, no per-visitor rows. Coarse referrer host and UA family only.

privacy_inventory.purpose: Derive pseudonymous client_hash for de-duplication and rate limiting
privacy_inventory.retention: Not persisted; used in-request only, immediately hashed
privacy_inventory.encryption: TLS in transit; never written to durable store in raw form
privacy_inventory.erasure_path: N/A — never stored raw; salt rotation invalidates derived hashes

privacy_inventory.purpose: Distinguish unique clicks and enforce rate limits without identifying users
privacy_inventory.encryption: Salted HMAC; salt stored in secrets manager and rotated periodically
privacy_inventory.erasure_path: Delete ClickEvent rows for a code or rotate salt to break linkage

privacy_inventory.purpose: Trace abusive link creators and scope link ownership
privacy_inventory.erasure_path: Cascade-delete with ShortLink on owner deletion request

i18n_plan.framework: ICU MessageFormat with gettext-style message keys
i18n_plan.rtl_strategy: Logical CSS properties and dir=auto on any HTML error/landing pages; RTL validated for ar
i18n_plan.notes: API is locale-agnostic in payloads; localization applies to error messages and any HTML pages via Accept-Language. long_url accepts IDN (punycode). Timestamps returned in ISO-8601 UTC with optional timezone param for stats.

open_questions: Should the same long_url always map to one code (idempotent/hash strategy) or always mint a new code? Affects generator choice and storage.
Do short links expire by default, and if so what TTL? Drives expires_at semantics and cleanup jobs.
Is authentication required to create links and/or view stats, or is the basic path anonymous? Determines auth module scope and stats authorization.
Is rate limiting required to be distributed (multi-instance) at launch, or is in-memory per-instance acceptable for v0?
What is the canonical short domain/host, and do we need custom-domain support?
Is a destination safety/blocklist check (e.g. Google Safe Browsing) in scope for iteration 0?

sections.title: Overview
sections.content: url-shortener: an API service to shorten URLs, redirect via short codes, collect privacy-preserving click stats, and enforce per-client rate limiting. Six modules: ApiGateway, ShortenerService, CodeGenerator, RedirectController, StatsCollector, RateLimiter, each behind a Protocol with explicit injection points.

sections.title: Module Boundaries
sections.content: ApiGateway routes+composes middleware. ShortenerService owns shorten/resolve domain logic. CodeGenerator is a pluggable code strategy (DIP/OCP). RedirectController handles GET /{code} and fires async click events. StatsCollector records and aggregates clicks. RateLimiter is a token-bucket guard with swappable store.

sections.title: Data Model
sections.content: ShortLink(code pk, long_url, created_at, expires_at?, creator_key_hash?, click_count). ClickEvent(id pk, code fk, occurred_at, client_hash?, referrer_host?, user_agent_family?). RateBucket(key pk, tokens, last_refill). No raw IPs persisted.

sections.title: Key Flows
sections.content: Shorten (POST /api/shorten, 1 request), Redirect (GET /{code}, async stats, <50ms p95), Stats (GET /api/stats/{code}, aggregates only). All flows pass through rate limiting.

sections.title: Architecture Decisions
sections.content: ADR-001 pluggable CodeGenerator behind Protocol (random-base62 default). ADR-002 async fire-and-forget click recording to protect redirect latency.

sections.title: Security & Privacy
sections.content: Top threats: malicious destination cloaking (scheme/host validation + 302), DoS (rate limiting + bounded retries + non-enumerable codes), PII disclosure via stats (HMAC IPs, aggregates only). PII minimized: raw IP never stored; client_hash 90-day retention; salt rotation as erasure lever.

sections.title: Open Questions
sections.content: Idempotent vs new code per URL; default expiry/TTL; auth requirement for create/stats; distributed vs in-memory rate limiting; canonical short domain; destination safety check scope.

sections.title: Digest
sections.content: url-shortener v0. Modules: ApiGateway, ShortenerService, CodeGenerator(Protocol, random-base62 default), RedirectController, StatsCollector, RateLimiter(token-bucket). Data: ShortLink, ClickEvent(pseudonymized client_hash, no raw IP), RateBucket. Flows: shorten(1 req,<200ms p95), redirect(<50ms p95, async stats), stats(aggregates only). Metric: 1-request shorten + sub-50ms redirect. ADR-001 pluggable code gen; ADR-002 async click recording. Threats: malicious-destination, DoS, PII disclosure — mitigated by scheme validation, rate limiting, HMAC IPs/aggregates. Privacy: raw IP never stored; 90-day click retention; salt-rotation erasure. Open Qs: idempotency, TTL, auth, distributed rate limiting, domain, safety check.
